subject: Post-call: Data access matrix, retention asks & next steps
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Elena Novik <elena@medisync.io>, Jorge Ramos <jorge.r@medisync.io>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 16:23:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Data access matrix, retention asks & next steps

Hi Elena / Jorge — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned:

Summary of must-haves you called out:
- 0-retention for PII (user identifiers, direct identifiers) for inference payloads in production
- EU residency for all persisted logs and backups
- Limited operational logs stored for 30 days only (audit trail)
- SOC 2 evidence and sample audit logs for procurement review

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) I attached a short matrix (redwood-data-retention-options.xlsx) with three presets we can pilot: "strict-ephemeral", "short-window-30d", "custom-ttl". Please review and mark your preference.
2) Karthik / Security: can you confirm feasibility of strict-ephemeral mode (0-retention for PII) in hosted Dedicated or Private?
3) Laura / Legal: if we can get a pilot exception, what contract language & limited-time SOW would you need to cover the audit/procurement ask?
4) Elena / Jorge: would you be available for a 30-minute alignment call next Tuesday to walk the procurement team through the matrix?

Attachment: redwood-data-retention-options.xlsx (spreadsheet — presets and technical notes)

Thanks — I’ll wait on your preference and will pull together a draft pilot plan.

—Marcus Lin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com
From: Elena Novik <elena@medisync.io>

Cc: Jorge Ramos <jorge.r@medisync.io>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 09:14:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Post-call: Data access matrix, retention asks & next steps

Thanks Marcus — concise and helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) 0-retention requirement applies to any field that contains direct patient identifiers or contact info. We can allow ephemeral caching for inference performance as long as it's never written to persistent logs.
2) Audit logs (who requested what, timestamps) are needed for 30 days for compliance; those logs must be stored in an EU region and encrypted with customer-managed keys if possible.
3) Procurement will ask for sample SOC 2 evidence and a short runbook of what you keep/for how long. Jorge is looping procurement — I attached our privacy template for quick reference.

We are open to a 6-week pilot under an exception with clear rollback if there are any issues. Tuesday next week 10:00 CET works for a demo of the matrix.

Attachment: medisync-privacy-template.docx

Best,
Elena Novik
Head of Product & Privacy | MediSync Health
elena@medisync.io

Forwarding Elena's clarifications — key asks: 0-retention for PII, EU residency + CMK for audit logs (30 days), SOC2 evidence.

Karthik: from a runtime + ops perspective, can we support a production configuration that: 
- persists zero PII fields to disk/logs,
- keeps only operational audit trail (non-PII) for 30 days in EU region (with optional CMK),
- provides technical evidence (sample logs with redacted values) for procurement?

Laura: if we can do a short-term exception/pilot, what contracting vehicle do you prefer — DP amendment, SOW, or a limited-scoped addendum? Also what risk approvals are needed to allow 0-retention in hosted/dedicated?

I propose a quick internal touchdown Monday morning so we can come back to Medisync with an executable pilot plan by EOD Monday.

—Marcus
From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Novik <elena@medisync.io>, Jorge Ramos <jorge.r@medisync.io>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 08:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Data access matrix, retention asks & next steps

Short answer: feasible with constraints. Notes below so commercial & legal know the tradeoffs.

Technical feasibility (hosted Dedicated / Private):
- We can configure request-processing to scrub and not persist any configured PII fields (names, emails, national IDs) before writing logs. This is an opt-in pipeline rule and can be enabled for specific customer IDs.
- "0-retention" for PII at the storage layer is possible if we guarantee no KV spill to durable storage — achievable in Private or Dedicated with strict runtime flags. For Hosted, we'd need a limited exception and extra guardrails.
- Audit logs: keeping non-PII operational logs for 30 days in an EU region is supported; we can enable customer-managed KMS to meet the CMK ask, but key-wrapping for live caches needs coordination.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: accidental PII capture via unstructured prompts (attachments/raw text). Mitigation: require a PII-scrubbing preprocessor (we can enable our redaction hook) and include it in pilot SOW.
- Risk: telemetry and error traces containing debug payloads. Mitigation: production telemetry will be configured to obfuscate payloads; retain only exception fingerprints.

Pilot proposal (6 weeks):
1) Week 0: Enable privacy pipeline + redaction hook for Medisync tenant in Dedicated EU region.
2) Weeks 1–4: Run production traffic with ephemeral-PII config; collect redacted audit samples; weekly check-ins.
3) Week 5: Security validation run (internal review + customer walkthrough of sample evidence).
4) Week 6: Decide scale / contract amendment or roll back.

I can provide a short tech appendix and sample redacted log output for procurement.

—Karthik Iyer
Senior Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
From: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Data access matrix, retention asks & next steps

Thanks — this is a good, pragmatic path forward. From a contracts perspective: 

Recommended vehicle: a short-term Addendum + Pilot SOW that sits under our Master Services Agreement. Key points to include:
- Scope: Medisync tenant in Dedicated EU cluster; pilot start/end dates; list of enabled runtime privacy features (redaction hook, no-persist for PII fields).
- Acceptance criteria: Security validation checklist and sign-off steps (Karthik to provide).
- Limited liability carveout for the pilot period; explicit rollback option and data wiping procedure.
- Confidentiality / audit evidence: we can provide redacted logs and SOC-2 summary; do not deliver raw PII under any circumstance.

I will draft an Addendum template and the SOW. Can Marcus share the completed spreadsheet preference from the customer? Once we have that, I’ll prepare a one-page risk memo for approvals (legal + security + product) and route for a 48-hour turnaround.

Attachment: sc-evidence-summary.pdf (internal summary of SOC2 artifacts we can share)

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com
